params.body:
gentells.com's front page showed a fixed number of posts, trends and reports: six posts under the lead, six trends, one report for a member, three for a visitor. The numbers were written into the site, so editors who order the trends and pin the lead in the Studio could not choose how much of each section a reader gets.

## Change

- `front_page_sizes` holds the editors' size per section. `getFrontSizes()` returns every size, falling back to the old amounts. `setFrontSizes()` takes only the values the site's layout carries:
  - posts under the lead: 3, 6, 9 or 12;
  - trends: 3, 6, 9 or 12;
  - a member's reports: 0 or 1;
  - a visitor's reports: 1 to 4.
- A visitor's three posts are a fixed design, so they are not a setting.
- `POST /site/front {sizes}` sets them from the Studio and pings the site's trends projection, as the trend order does.
- `GET /site/trends` adds `front` and `frontChoices`. The projection's trend payload adds `front`.

## Order

This is safe to merge first: the site and the Studio ignore the new fields until their own PRs land.

## Checked

- `test/front-page-order.test.mjs`: defaults, a partial set, and a refused value changing nothing. 11 of 11 pass.
- Full suite: 1152 of 1158 pass. The 6 failures are `report-render`, which fail the same way on main here because the workbench has no PDF tools.
params.title: Front page sizes: editors set how many posts, trends and reports gentells.com shows
